title: Electrical Engineer
description:
Highly motivated transformer Test Engineer to perform electrical testing, diagnosis, and condition assessment of oil-filled power and distribution transformers and associated high-voltage equipment. The candidate will be responsible for executing factory acceptance tests (FAT), field acceptance tests, troubleshooting, and technical analysis. This includes developing test plans, performing various tests such as insulation and dielectric testing, turns ratio, power factor, and sweep frequency if needed, excitation current, and bushing tests. The role also emphasizes adherence to international standards, safety procedures, and efficient testing operations.

Ensure compliance with IEEE standards and that all testing procedures meet international and national standards (IEC, ANSI) and customer specifications.

* **Test Planning:** Develop and implement detailed test plans and procedures for transformers and electrical equipment.
* Maintain up-to-date calibrated instruments.
* **Quality Control:** Ensure quality control measures are followed during testing to detect any defects or non-conformance.
* **Root Cause Analysis:** Investigate failures during testing, determine root causes, and recommend corrective actions.
* **Documentation:** Accurately record test results, observations, and discrepancies, generating detailed test reports.
* Testing: Analyze transformer oil to assess its quality, dielectric strength, DGA, and suitability for use in the transformer.
* **Collaboration:** Collaborate with design, engineering, and RD teams to provide feedback for product improvements and design optimizations.
* **Safety Compliance**: Adhere to and audit safety protocols during all testing activities to ensure a safe working environment.
* **Training:** Provide training to technicians on testing methods, safety practices, and operational procedures.

description:

title: SCADA Programming Manager
description:
As the **SCADA / Programming Manager**, you will be responsible for the technical management, programming, maintenance, and operational sustainment of mission-critical facility control systems supporting Intelligence Community (IC) operations. This position provides technical leadership and oversight of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Building Management Systems (BMS), network infrastructure, software applications, and bulk energy storage systems.

The SCADA / Programming Manager ensures the continued reliability, availability, integrity, and operational readiness of critical facility infrastructure in support of intelligence mission requirements. The position operates within a 24-hour, 7-day-a-week mission environment and requires close coordination with mission operations, facility engineering, information technology, cybersecurity, and other operational stakeholders.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Provide technical management and oversight of SCADA systems, PLCs, BMS platforms, and associated facility automation and control infrastructure.
* Manage the programming, configuration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and optimization of complex facility control systems supporting mission-critical operations.
* Oversee PLC programming logic development, modifications, testing, and sustainment to ensure reliable system performance and operational continuity.
* Manage the configuration, programming, maintenance, and patching of network switches and supporting software systems associated with facility control networks.
* Oversee the operational sustainment and technical performance of bulk energy storage systems and associated control infrastructure.
* Ensure facility control systems remain operationally available and capable of supporting continuous Intelligence Community mission requirements.

title: Data Center Security Manager, DC Security
description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon Web Services (AWS) serves customers and developers who rely on storage, compute, and our other service capabilities. Our customers trust us to handle their data with air-tight security measures, which is something that we guarantee.  
  
AWS is growing rapidly, and we are looking for a Data Center Security Manager to join our expanding Infrastructure Operations team.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
As a Data Center Security Manager you will be tasked with driving operational security excellence in several separate facilities located within a short driving distance. Your constant vigilance will discover physical security gaps and shortcomings, which you will drive to fix immediately. You will interface and direct vendors involved in new security construction, repairs, daily security operations and patrols, and planning. You will extract metrics and observe improvements by looking at hard data. You will make suggestions on improving electronic surveillance and access controls. You will direct efforts to educate data center occupants on false alarm reductions. You will write and implement security process and procedures. Your position will require you to write reports, create presentations and communicate with management on the status of physical security operations.  
  
A day in the life  
Your day begins with a walkthrough of your assigned site, checking that access control systems, cameras, and intrusion detection hardware are functioning properly. You review overnight incident reports and triage incoming operational tickets, prioritizing items that need immediate attention. You meet with contract security vendors to review performance metrics and approve work activities that may affect physical security. You also collaborate with data center operations teams to address emerging issues, document findings, and refine standard operating procedures.

title: Sr Applied Scientist, Embedded Battery Algorithms, Energy Storage
description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Do you want to write the algorithms that control next-generation batteries, and shape the future of energy storage? This role sits where electrochemistry, data/ML, and control theory meet. You will develop the physics-informed and data-driven methods that estimate state of charge, health, power capability, and remaining life, and validate them against lab and fleet data until they are ready to ship. Your algorithms will decide how hard a battery can be pushed, when it needs attention, and how long it will last, so they shape the safety, warranty, and economics of the whole product. You will work side by side with cell, systems, and software engineers, and as an early hire you will help define how we develop and validate battery algorithms.  
  
This role can be based in Boston, Irvine, Sunnyvale, or Seattle, and involves occasional domestic and international travel, up to 10% of the time.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Develop and own algorithms for state of charge, state of health, power capability, and remaining useful life, combining physics-based models with data-driven and estimation methods.
* Deliver validated reference implementations, test vectors, and accuracy targets that define what production code must achieve.
* Design the test plans and data needed to develop and validate algorithms, working with the cell and testing teams to turn lab and field data into model improvements.
* Analyze algorithm performance across the deployed fleet, find where models drift or fail, and drive improvements.
* Own the accuracy and robustness of battery algorithms, and sign off that production implementations match the validated reference. Provide algorithm evidence for safety certification.

Your week moves between data, models, and experiments. One day you might be working out why a health estimate drifts on cells that have aged in the field, and the next deciding which model structure holds accuracy at cold tem
